skills.name: Ultrastructure of plant and animal cells

note.text:
Under the electron microscope cells show many organelles:
• Nucleus: contains DNA, controls the cell. • Mitochondria: aerobic respiration, release energy. • Ribosomes: make proteins.
• Endoplasmic reticulum (ER): transport channels; rough ER has ribosomes. • Golgi body: packages and secretes substances.
• Cell membrane: partially permeable, controls entry and exit. • Cytoplasm: where most reactions happen.
Only in plant cells: cellulose cell wall (support), chloroplasts (photosynthesis), large permanent vacuole with cell sap.
Animal cells have small temporary vacuoles and centrioles (used in cell division).

sections.heading: Seeing more detail
sections.text:
With a light microscope you see the cell wall, membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole and chloroplasts. An electron microscope magnifies much more and shows the ultrastructure: many tiny organelles, each with a job.
• Nucleus: holds the DNA and controls the cell.
• Mitochondria: aerobic respiration releases energy.
• Ribosomes: make proteins.
• Endoplasmic reticulum: a network of channels; rough ER is covered in ribosomes.
• Golgi body: packages substances for export.

sections.heading: Plant cells
Animal cells
sections.text:
Animal cells have a membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, ER and Golgi, but no cell wall, no chloroplasts and only small temporary vacuoles. They have centrioles, which help in cell division.
Cells that do a lot of work have more of certain organelles: muscle cells are packed with mitochondria; gland cells with ribosomes and Golgi bodies.

key_words.meaning: a structure with a particular job inside a cell
letting some substances through but not others

mistake.wrong: Plant cells do not have mitochondria because they have chloroplasts
mistake.right: Plant cells have both: they photosynthesise and also respire
mistake.why: All living cells respire, day and night, so plant cells need mitochondria too.

worked_example.problem: Give three differences between a palisade cell of a leaf and a cell from the lining of your cheek.
steps: The leaf cell has a cellulose cell wall; the cheek cell has only a cell membrane.
The leaf cell has chloroplasts; the cheek cell has none.
The leaf cell has a large permanent vacuole; the cheek cell has only small temporary vacuoles.
worked_example.answer: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole in the plant cell only

cards.idea: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
example: Animal cells have none of these.

pick.q: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
pick.y: Only plant cells have a cellulose cell wall.

pick.q: Which structure is found in both plant and animal cells?
e: Only plant cells have a cell wall.
Animal cells have only small vacuoles.

pick.q: Which structure is found in animal cells but not in most plant cells?
e: The cell wall is a plant structure.

questions.prompt: In the drawing of a plant cell, which letter labels the {plantPart(i)}?

pick.q: Which cells would have the most mitochondria?
pick.r: muscle cells, which need a lot of energy
e: Mature red blood cells have no mitochondria.

pick.q: A cell makes and sends out many enzymes (proteins). Which organelles will it have many of?
pick.r: ribosomes, rough ER and Golgi bodies
pick.y: Proteins are made on ribosomes, moved by rough ER and packaged by Golgi.

pick.q: Root hair cells have no chloroplasts. Why?
pick.r: They are underground, where there is no light for photosynthesis
pick.y: Chloroplasts would be useless in the dark.

pick.q: A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria, a cellulose wall and chloroplasts. It is…
e: Animal cells have no cell wall or chloroplasts.
A virus is not a cell.

pick.q: A cell has DNA free in the cytoplasm, a cell wall and no mitochondria. It is…
e: Plant cells have a nucleus and mitochondria.
Animal cells have a nucleus and no wall.
Yeast is a eukaryote with a nucleus.
pick.y: No nucleus and no mitochondria: prokaryote.

pick.q: Why is the cell membrane described as partially permeable?
pick.r: It lets some substances through but not others
e: Then it could not control entry.
Then the cell could not take in food or oxygen.
pick.y: It controls which substances enter and leave.
